definition: A place on the edge or in the vicinity of something; especially an outlying district or a familiar haunt.
etymology: It began as Anglo-French puralee: land released from the restrictions of a royal forest, probably literally a place one could go freely. In English, the freed forest edge became any bordering territory—or the circles one frequents.
usage: By late September, the hedgerow paths and orchard lanes become the most inviting purlieus of the town.
